clue.text: What Zola famously did in L' Aurore

definitions.text: What Zola famously did in L' Aurore

parts.words: What Zola famously did in L' Aurore
parts.note: Zola's 1898 open letter in the newspaper L'Aurore was headlined ..., charging the army over the Dreyfus affair

explanation.surface: A question about Emile Zola's most famous act of journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's letter charged named officers with wrongdoing, which is to lay blame formally.

clue.text: Prime nature with an added (Browning, The Ring and the Book)

definitions.text: Prime nature with an added (Browning, The Ring and the Book)

parts.words: Prime nature with an added (Browning, The Ring and the Book)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Browning's poem speaks of prime nature with an added craftsmanship of the poet

explanation.surface: A quotation from Browning's long poem with its last word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Browning's line names the poet's skill, the craft added to raw nature.

clue.text: With Steinbeck it preceded a row

definitions.text: With Steinbeck it preceded a row

parts.words: With Steinbeck it preceded a row
parts.note: Steinbeck's novel title is this word followed by Row, a Monterey street of fish-packing plants

explanation.surface: Something that, in Steinbeck's hands, came before a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is the street in Steinbeck's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's novel takes its name from a street of fish-canning factories in Monterey.

clue.text: Direction fit for canonized poet

parts.note: south is a compass direction
fit as in healthy means well

explanation.surface: A compass bearing suited to a poet who was made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Southwell was an Elizabethan Jesuit poet, martyred in 1595 and canonized in 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jesuit martyr Robert Southwell wrote devotional verse and was declared a saint in 1970.

clue.text: Histrionic cop. Irate? Could be

indicators.note: the letters of cop and irate could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: An angry policeman is putting on a theatrical display.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone emotional display is likened to grand opera, so the adjective means melodramatic.

clue.text: She shared a car, it appears, with maker of 9

definitions.text: She shared a car, it appears, with maker of 9

parts.words: She shared a car, it appears, with maker of 9
parts.note: the Yorkshire novelist's surname is that of a luxury car marque and of E. C. Bentley, author of the detective novel at 9

explanation.surface: A woman seems to have carpooled with a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shared a car' means she has the same name as the car make, and 'maker of 9' is the author of 9-down, E. C. Bentley.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis Bentley was a Yorkshire novelist whose surname matches both the car and E. C. Bentley.

clue.text: French novel from Italy

definitions.meaning: the French word for a novel
of the city of Rome, hence Italian

explanation.surface: A piece of French fiction that comes from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The French call a novel a roman, and the English adjective means belonging to Rome.

clue.text: The ones here (American) recall a duke of Athens

parts.note: these means the ones here, pointing at nearby things

explanation.surface: These Americans are reminded of a Greek nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recall' is only a link here: the pieces bring the duke to mind. Shakespeare calls Theseus Duke of Athens in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Midsummer Night's Dream the legendary Athenian king is styled a duke.

clue.text: Some of Dreiser's stories are linked, it seems

definitions.text: Some of Dreiser's stories are linked, it seems

parts.words: Some of Dreiser's stories are linked, it seems
parts.note: Dreiser's 1927 story collection has a title meaning a series of connected links

explanation.surface: Several of Theodore Dreiser's short stories appear to be connected.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Dreiser's collection names connected metal links, hence 'linked'.

clue.text: Detective's final valise identified by woman in black in the States

definitions.text: Detective's final valise identified by woman in black in the States

parts.words: Detective's final valise identified by woman in black in the States
parts.note: E. C. Bentley's detective novel, whose title reads as an investigator's last suitcase, appeared in America as The Woman in Black

explanation.surface: A sleuth's last suitcase is picked out by a woman dressed in black in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'valise' plays on 'case', and the American edition of the novel was titled The Woman in Black.
explanation.definitionFit: Bentley's novel is named for the final investigation of its detective Philip Trent.

clue.text: He took on two wives. But only in play

definitions.text: He took on two wives. But only in play

parts.words: He took on two wives. But only in play
parts.note: Pinero's play The Second Mrs ... is named after a man's second marriage, so on stage he had two wives in turn

explanation.surface: A man who married twice, but only on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two wives' sounds like bigamy; Pinero's play title means he married a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrey in Pinero's The Second Mrs Tanqueray takes Paula as his second wife.

clue.text: Graduate with a long time to identify mythical canine suicide

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A graduate with plenty of time works out which legendary dog killed itself.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarius's dog led his daughter to his body, then killed itself from grief.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithful hound of Icarius drowned itself in grief in Greek legend, a dog that took its own life.

clue.text: Hero of Irish novel, posthumously published

definitions.text: Hero of Irish novel, posthumously published

parts.words: Hero of Irish novel, posthumously published
parts.note: Joyce's early novel, printed after his death, has the word Hero in its title after its protagonist's first name

explanation.surface: Naming the protagonist of an Irish novel issued after its author died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is both the protagonist and part of the title Stephen Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Dedalus is the central figure of Joyce's Stephen Hero, published in 1944.

clue.text: How Allbeury shed light on the web?

definitions.text: How Allbeury shed light on the web?

parts.words: How Allbeury shed light on the web?
parts.note: Ted Allbeury's spy novel is The ... Network, its first word a portable lamp

explanation.surface: Asking how a spy novelist illuminated the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the web' reads as the internet but is the Network of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp sheds light, and it is the first word of Allbeury's The Lantern Network.

clue.text: May be royal, feminine or masculine, weak and imperfect and part of a scheme

definitions.text: May be royal, feminine or masculine, weak and imperfect and part of a scheme

parts.words: May be royal, feminine or masculine, weak and imperfect and part of a scheme
parts.note: all are terms of prosody: a royal stanza, feminine and masculine endings, weak and imperfect matches, and a pattern of line endings

explanation.surface: Describing something royal, of either sex, feeble, flawed and part of a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads like a person or plotter, but each is a verse term: rhyme royal, feminine and masculine rhyme, weak and imperfect rhyme, rhyme scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets speak of rhyme royal, feminine, masculine, weak and imperfect forms, and a rhyme scheme.

clue.text: Essential thriller-writer's standby missing from Sayers's Hangman Holiday?

definitions.text: Essential thriller-writer's standby missing from Sayers's Hangman Holiday?

parts.words: Essential thriller-writer's standby missing from Sayers's Hangman Holiday?
parts.note: the tension every thriller needs, and also hanging, which a hangman on holiday would not be doing

explanation.surface: Wondering what key thriller ingredient Dorothy L. Sayers left out of a story collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means tension but also the state of being hung up, which a hangman's holiday lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrillers depend on anxious uncertainty, and the word also suggests hanging suspended.

clue.text: Giant moon of Saturn

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth one of the Giants who fought the gods, buried under Etna
an icy satellite of Saturn named after that Giant

explanation.surface: A huge moon orbiting Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Giant of myth crushed under Etna lent his name to Saturn's sixth-largest satellite.

clue.text: Early viticulturist and good-time Charlie

definitions.meaning: the Greek god who first taught mortals to grow vines
a pleasure-seeker, as the god of revelry was

explanation.surface: A pioneering wine-grower who loves a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of wine taught vine-growing and presided over drunken revels.

clue.text: Upset a north-eastern crime writer

parts.note: to upset a glass is to spill it

explanation.surface: A crime novelist from the north-east is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal or an adjective, but it is the verb SPILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Spillane wrote the hard-boiled Mike Hammer thrillers.

clue.text: Fellow in agony could be Ganelon

indicators.note: the word for a fellow is placed in the word for agony

parts.note: agony is pain
a lad is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in torment might be the traitor of the Charlemagne legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganelon, who betrays Roland in the Chanson de Roland, was one of Charlemagne's twelve peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganelon was one of Charlemagne's twelve peers, the knightly champions of the legend.

clue.text: Firbank's whim places church on this island

indicators.note: the clue says church is placed on the island's name to give Firbank's title, so taking church away leaves the island

parts.note: Ronald Firbank's novel Caprice; a caprice is a whim
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Firbank's fancy builds a church on an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: adding CE to the island gives CAPRICE, Firbank's 1917 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Bay of Naples is the one meant by 'this island'.

clue.text: Artist who produced Palace of Pleasure

definitions.meaning: William ... compiled The Palace of Pleasure, a 1566 collection of tales

explanation.surface: The creator of a pleasure palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is an artist, and William Painter compiled the Elizabethan story collection.

clue.text: Revolting Fleming celebrated by Goethe and Beethoven

definitions.text: Revolting Fleming celebrated by Goethe and Beethoven

parts.words: Revolting Fleming celebrated by Goethe and Beethoven
parts.note: a Flemish count who resisted Spanish rule, subject of Goethe's play and Beethoven's overture

explanation.surface: A disgusting Fleming praised by two great Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebellious, not disgusting; Lamoral, Count of Egmont was beheaded in 1568.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish count who led opposition to Spain was dramatised by Goethe and scored by Beethoven.

clue.text: Attentive to ladies as George Sand's lords

definitions.meaning: Sand's novel appeared in English as The ... Lords of Bois-Dore

explanation.surface: Being courteous to women in the manner of George Sand's noblemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtly man attentive to women is described with this word, as in Sand's English title.

clue.text: Academician returns to any kind of parent language

indicators.note: the abbreviation for an Academician returns, so it is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: any kind of means the letters of any in some other form

explanation.surface: An art academician goes back to a sort of mother tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RA into AR; 'kind of' rearranges ANY into YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteenth-century philologists used the term for the reconstructed ancestor of the Indo-European tongues.

clue.text: Not like new philologist

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of not like make something new

explanation.surface: A language scholar unlike anything fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: J. R. R. Tolkien was Oxford professor of Anglo-Saxon and of English language.

clue.text: Oliphant's and Simon's couples thus suited

definitions.text: Oliphant's and Simon's couples thus suited

parts.words: Oliphant's and Simon's couples thus suited
parts.note: Neil Simon's pair were The Odd Couple, and Oliphant wrote of strangely matched pairs

explanation.surface: Pairs from two writers that are mismatched in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who are strangely matched are peculiarly suited, as in Simon's play.

clue.text: Karen Blixen's were fateful

parts.note: Blixen, writing as Isak Dinesen, published a collection called ... of Destiny

explanation.surface: Karen Blixen's short tales carried a sense of fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tales are what the title of Blixen's Anecdotes of Destiny calls her stories.

clue.text: Occupied, like Wildfell Hall

definitions.meaning: Anne Bronte's novel is The Tenant of Wildfell Hall, so the hall had someone renting it

explanation.surface: Lived in, like the house in Anne Bronte's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that is let has a renter, as Bronte's hall did.

clue.text: Very big flower for Egyptian god

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big
the iris is a flower

explanation.surface: An enormous bloom offered to an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian ruler of the dead and the afterlife.
